reason.delayTooShort: Under EU 261, compensation starts at a delay of 3 hours or more.

reason.medium: Flight 1,500–3,500 km (or any intra-EU flight above 1,500 km) — €400 per passenger.
reason.longReduced: Non-EU flight over 3,500 km with a 3–4 hour delay — reduced €300 (Art. 7(2)).
reason.long: Non-EU flight over 3,500 km with a delay of 4+ hours — €600 per passenger.

long.desc: Long-haul non-EU flights delayed over 4 hours.

items.q: How far back can I claim?
items.a: In the Czech Republic you can typically claim EU 261 compensation for flights up to three years in the past; in some countries even longer.

items.q: What if the airline blames the delay on something else?
items.a: The airline must prove 'extraordinary circumstances' (severe weather, a third-party strike, a security risk). Technical faults and ordinary operational issues don't qualify.
The calculator is free. If you use our claim service, we take a share only from the amount we successfully recover.

items.q: Does this apply to low-cost carriers?
items.a: Yes. EU 261 covers all airlines departing from the EU and all EU carriers flying into the EU. The ticket price doesn't matter.
The rules are similar. If the airline informed you late or didn't offer a reasonable alternative, you may be entitled to compensation. Contact us and we'll review your case.

footer.tagline: The fast way to compensation for delayed flights.
footer.disclaimer: Amounts shown are an estimate based on EU Regulation 261/2004. The final claim depends on the specific circumstances of the flight.
